<xref rid="A00083"> הָלַךְ)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>going, going away; walking; run</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pes. 8
<sup>b</sup> בהֲלִיכָתָן on their going (opp. חזירה, return). Keth. 111

<sup>b</sup> bot. שגְזֵלֹו מן הה', read: ההֲלָכָה, v. Y. Keth. II, end, 27
<sup>a</sup>.]—
<plural-form>Pl. הֲלִיכוֹת</plural-form>. Meg. 28
<sup>b</sup>; Nidd. 73
<sup>a</sup>, v. הֲלָכָה.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="E00561">
<head-word>הָלַךְ</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to go, go away; to walk</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 84
<sup>a</sup> כשהָלַכְתִּי וכ' when I left home to study with &c. Macc. 10
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. בדרך שאדם רוצה לֵילֵךְ בה מוֹלִיכִין אותו whatever way one desires to go, one is led; a. v. fr.—הֹולְכֵי מדברות travellers through the desert. Taan. 27
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.—Y. Kidd. I, 61
<sup>d</sup> כהולכים בתורת ד' (not בה') as though they did walk in the law &c.—Imper. לֵךְ, לְכָה, v. כָּלָה 
<italic>Pi.</italic>, a. כַּלֵּךְ.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִילֵּךְ, הִלֵּךְ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> same, same, 
<italic>to walk, tread upon</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. IX, 2 (122
<sup>a</sup>) או שהי' בהן (Mish. ed. שהלך) or trod upon them for tanning purposes. Erub. 100
<sup>b</sup> שיְהַלֵּךְ ע"ג וכ' to tread upon plants. Gen. R. s. 39 מְהַלֵּךְ בארם וכ' travelling through Aram &c.—Keth. 60
<sup>a</sup>; Ker. 22
<sup>a</sup> מְהַלְּכֵי שתים 
<pgbrk id="pg353" />walking on two legs (human beings); a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to cause opening of the bowels</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Kil. I, 27
<sup>a</sup> top מְהַלֶּכֶת את בני מיעים; cmp. הִילּוּךְ. [Y. Keth. XII, 35
<sup>b</sup> top מהלך לפניהן אל הארץ, v. חָלַד.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הוֹלִיךְ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to lead; to carry</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Macc. 10
<sup>b</sup>, v. supra. Gitt. 4
<sup>a</sup> המוֹלִיךְ וכ' he who carries abroad a letter of divorce, contrad. to המביא he who brings a letter from abroad. Ab. Zar. III, 9 יוֹלִיךְ הנאה וכ' let him cast the profit (one loaf’s value) into the Sea. Gitt. VI, 1 הוֹלֵךְ גט וכ' carry this letter of divorce (as a messenger). Ib. 63
<sup>a</sup> sq. (distinction between הילך, here is the letter of divorce, i.e. take possession of it in behalf of my wife, and הולך carry it, i.e. be my messenger). Ib. 64
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. הולך כזכי דמי ‘carry’ (the letter of divorce) is equal to ‘take possession’ (in behalf of her who authorized thee); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְהַלֵּךְ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to go away, withdraw</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Cant. R. to V, 1; Gen. R. s. 19 (ref. to Gen. III, 8) מְהַלֵּךְ … אלא מִתְהַלֵּךְ וכ' it does not say 
<italic>m’hallekh</italic> (walking) but 
<italic>mith-hallekh</italic>, He hastened and went upward. Ib. מתהלך לו (ed. מת הלך, corr. acc., v. Matt. K.) is he (Adam) going away (from God)?, v. אתמהא.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="E00566">
<head-word>הֲלָכָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (הלך) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (cmp. מִנְהָג) 
<italic>practice, adopted opinion, rule</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—ה' כ־ in practice, the opinion of … is the rule. Keth. 77
<sup>a</sup> ה' כמותו; a. v. fr.—ה' למשה מסיני a usage dating from Moses as delivered from Sinai, i.e. 
<italic>a traditional law</italic> or 
<italic>a traditional interpretation of a written law</italic>. Kidd. 38
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> in gen. 
<italic>traditional law, tradition, custom.</italic></definition>
<notes> Orl. III, 9 הערלה ה' the application of the laws of Orlah (v. עָרְלָה) outside of Palestine is traditional or a custom (הילכות מדינה, v. Kidd. 38
<sup>b</sup>).—Y. Bets. II, 61
<sup>b</sup> top לה' as a traditional opinion (of a teacher), opp. לעובדא as his own decision for practice. Y. Dem. III, 23
<sup>c</sup> bot., sq. מה' according to a custom. Ker. 13
<sup>b</sup> ‘which the Lord has spoken’ (Lev. X, 11) זו ה' that means traditional interpretations. Ib. III, 9 (15
<sup>b</sup>) אם ה' נקבל אם לדין וכ' if it is a tradition, we must accept it, but if it is a logical inference, there may be an objection to it.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>law</italic>, contrad. to אֲגָדָה.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 31
<sup>a</sup> מתוך דבר ה' from discussion about a law, opp. ה' פסוקה a decision arrived at after discussion. Ib. 47
<sup>b</sup> המחדדין … בה' who whet each other’s wits in legal discussion. Snh. 82
<sup>a</sup> נתעלמה ממנו ה' the law had escaped his memory. Ib. ראה … ונזכר ה' he saw an act and recalled the law; a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. הֲלָכוֹת,</plural-form> constr. הִלְכוֹת, הִילְ'. Kidd. l. c. הי' מדינה (v. R. S. to Orl. III, 9; ed. הלכתא מדינה, corr. acc.) the usages of the country (outside of Palestine). Y. Hor. III, end, 48
<sup>c</sup> אילו ה' that means the collections of laws (Mishnah). Tem. 14
<sup>b</sup> כותבי ה' those who reduce traditions (oral law) to writing. Snh. 67
<sup>b</sup> הי' כשפים the laws concerning the punishment of witchcraft. Ib. הלְ' יצירה mystic practices. Sabb. 32
<sup>a</sup>; Tosef. ib. II, 10; a. v. fr.—[הלכה in Talmud Y., heading of 
<italic>Mishnah</italic>, in Talm. Bab. מתני'.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<plural-form>Pl. הִלְכָאתָא, הִילְכָתָא</plural-form>. Ib. XXVI, 7 (ed. Wil. הַלְכְתָא). Ib. XXIX, 5; a. e.—Targ. Ps. XXIII, 3 הִלְכְוָותָא ד־ Ms. (ed. Lag. הִילְכְוָת צ', ed. Wil. הִלְכַת).</notes></sense>

<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. למאי ה' for what practical issue &c.?—
<plural-form>Pl. הִלְכָתָא</plural-form>. Ber. 31
<sup>a</sup>, v. גִּיבַּר; a. fr.—Targ. Koh. XII, 11 הִילְכְתִין.—Lev. R. s. 3, beg. בר הִילְכָן (fr. הִילְכָא) a scholar.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="E00571">
<head-word>הִלֵּל, </head-word>
<head-word>הִילֵּ'</head-word>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>Hillel</italic>, 1) H.</definition>
<notes>, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>

<notes> Pes. 66
<sup>a</sup>. Tosef. Snh. VII, 11. Yoma 35
<sup>b</sup> ה' מחייב וכ' the example of Hillel condemns the poor (who plead poverty as an excuse for not studying the Law); a. v. fr.—בֵּית ה' 
<italic>Beth-Hillel, the School of H., the Hillelites</italic>. Bets. I, 1; a. v. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition />
<notes> H., son of Rabban Gamliel. Pes. 51
<sup>a</sup>; Tosef. M. Kat. II, 16; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition />
<notes> R. H., son of אָלָס or וָולָס, an Amora. Y. Kil. IX, 32
<sup>a</sup> top. Gitt. 59
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—[Y. Bets. V, 63
<sup>a</sup> bot. ר' ליל, prob. a corrupt. or abbrev. of H.]</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition />
<notes> name of several Amoraim. Y. Ber. II, 5
<sup>a</sup> bot.; a. fr. V. Frank. M’bo p. 76
<sup>a</sup></notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—5)</number>
<definition />
<notes> one Rabbi H. Snh. 98
<sup>b</sup>, sq.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="E00573">
<head-word>הַלֵּל</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced.)
